chapter: Moving, Columbia Missouri and leaving home
title: Wanting out: black migration north
summary: Thompson looked for a way out of the town and sees his thinking as part of the black migration out of the South.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: So it was because of this particular incident that I desperately tried to find some way to get out of that town, to go there where I thought things were better, you know.

And of course, naturally, there were thousands of other black people like me who naturally had to think this way, which probably accounts for why so many black people migrated from the deep south to the north, where it was supposed to be a little more opportunity and more leniency in the social structure. Now,this happened to turn out to be a question or the whole situation turned out to be questionable to me later when I found out that that wasn't necessarily the case.

However, not having studied sociology or the science of sociology and those things, I didn't consider myself to be that capable of figuring it out. In fact at my age, as far as I was concerned, there wasn't enough time to sit down and figure out what was right or wrong, or what I should do. All
I knew was that my fear of this situation, and my lack of desire to want to be in it, made me think about trying to get out of there.
